expectations.text: Rejects the claim that registration friction drives no-shows.
expectations.evidence: "The evidence behind the skill says the link is mostly a confound."

expectations.text: States that among paid events, no-show rates stay roughly flat at about 16-19% regardless of how easy or hard registration is.
expectations.evidence: "paid events show flat no-show rates of about 16-19%. This holds whether registration completes at 65% or 98%."

expectations.text: Names the confound: free events also tend to run the simplest registration forms, so controlling for the free-versus-paid split erases the apparent correlation.
expectations.evidence: "Free events run the simplest forms... Controlling for free versus paid removes the effect."

expectations.text: Identifies the 100%-at-two-weeks and 200%-at-one-week figures as a registration signup curve that tells a marketing plan whether registrations are on pace.
expectations.evidence: "a marketing pace chart... tells you whether registrations are on pace."

expectations.text: States that this curve is not an overbooking instruction, and routes it to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-marketing-plan.
expectations.evidence: "It doesn't tell you how many to accept, and it belongs to event-marketing-plan."

expectations.text: Distinguishes the signup curve from the separate show-up trendline that does set the overbooking multiplier.
expectations.evidence: "The curve and the ceiling are two different instructions."; "about 50% of registrants show up"

expectations.text: Recommends against adding the five-question form and mandatory confirmation click as a no-show fix.
expectations.evidence: "Do not add the five-question form and mandatory confirmation click to fix no-shows."

expectations.text: States a registration ceiling of 240 for the 120-seat workshop, derived from the free-event show-up rate.
Does not blend the signup curve percentages with any show-up rate or drop-off range.
